newsitem.title: USA: Jailed Black Panther leader to get new trial.
newsitem.headline: Jailed Black Panther leader to get new trial.

text.p: Former Black Panther leader Elmer "Geronimo" Pratt, convicted of murder 25 years ago and designated a "prisoner of conscience" by Amnesty International, was granted a new trial Thursday.
Orange County Superior Court Judge Everett Dickey ruled that Pratt should be retried because he was convicted mainly on the evidence of an FBI informant.

"It is reasonably probable that (Pratt) could have obtained a different result in the entire absence of (the informant's) testimony," the judge wrote in his judgment in Santa Ana, some 40 miles (70 km) south of Los Angeles.
The Los Angeles district attorney's office, which had fought Pratt's request for a new trial, released a terse statement saying it had not yet decided whether to appeal the judge's ruling.

Pratt was convicted in 1972 of shooting a schoolteacher in Santa Monica and wounding her husband. He has always proclaimed his innocence, saying he was 400 miles (640 km) away in Oakland at the time of the killing in 1968 and that the FBI knew, because he was under surveillance.
His lawyer, Johnnie Cochran, who won O.J. Simpson's acquittal on murder charges in 1995, has campaigned for two decades to get Pratt a new trial.

According to the weekly newspaper L.A. Weekly, Federal Bureau of Investigation documents recently made public showed that the prosecution's chief witness against Pratt, ex-Panther Julius Carl Butler, had been an informant for the bureau.
Pratt learned after his conviction through the Freedom of Information Act, the FBI targeted him for "neutralization."

At the height of the militant black power movement of the late 1960's, J. Edgar Hoover's FBI had set up a counter-intelligence programme to destroy the Panthers and other groups labeled "subversive," the newspaper said.
It also said FBI records later made public showed the bureau withheld wiretap information that would have substantiated Pratt's alibi he was in Oakland.
